title: Servicing Academy Q&A: Lateness Scaling of Good-Faith Days on Deferral Qualifying Payments
content:
**What is a good-faith amount?** A deferral qualifying payment on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts also carries a good-faith amount, applied to principal, equal to one day's interest on the principal balance at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis multiplied by the good-faith days and rounded to the cent.

**How does the lateness record affect it?** The good-faith days are scaled by the lateness record, counting the late fees assessed on the contract when fewer than 12 whole months separate their assessment date from the payment date. The scaling is applied to the good-faith days once every day added to or taken off them has been counted:

| Late fees in the 12-month window | Good-faith days |
|---|---|
| three or more | multiplied by the heavy-lateness multiplier, 2.0 |
| exactly two | multiplied by the two-late multiplier, 1.5 |
| one or none | taken as they stand |

**Is the result rounded to whole days?** No. The scaled days are used as they come out; the rounding to the cent happens once, on the good-faith amount.

**How is the window counted?** A late fee assessed on 2025-11-20 is 11 whole months before a payment on 2026-11-19 and counts; it is 12 whole months before a payment on 2026-11-20 and does not.

**A worked figure?** Hypothetical: 15 good-faith days with exactly two late fees in the window become 22.5 days; on a principal balance of 9800.00 at 15.59 percent over a 365-day basis that gives a good-faith amount of 94.18. With three late fees the same 15 days become 30 days, 125.57.
